subject: Behavior-preserving restructuring of existing code — extracting functions, reducing duplication, renaming for clarity,…

evals.prompt: Define refactor in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the refactor skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind refactor. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "the test is failing after my edit — what did I break?". Should refactor activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force refactor onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to semantics, tool-call-flow, generative-ui, context-graph, error-boundary, performance-testing, debugging, testing-strategy.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "this 600-line function is hard to reason about — decompose it while keeping tests green". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying refactor.

Place refactor among its adjacent skills (semantics, tool-call-flow, generative-ui, context-graph, error-boundary, performance-testing, debugging, testing-strategy). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about refactor and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
